golden: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
candidates: getClientsWithPermission iterates all resources of type Clients, which includes the schema 'all-clients' resource whose name is also Clients; returning that value can break call sites that treat results as client IDs (e.g. realm.getClientById(cid) in AvailableRoleMappingResource). Consider excluding the resource-type entry (where resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) from the returned set.

Test uses getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) without asserting the list has at least 2 elements, which can make it flaky if the default client-scope set changes. Consider asserting a minimum size (or selecting a scope deterministically) before indexing.

golden: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
candidates: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses groupResource.getId() (authz resource id) as if it were the Keycloak group id; hasPermission() also expects an identifier that can be resolved via resourceStore.findByName() (i.e., the resource name). This likely breaks group-scoped user visibility and can populate UserModel.GROUPS with unusable identifiers.

canManage() falls back to hasPermission(... VIEW, MANAGE), which means a principal with only view on Groups could satisfy auth.groups().requireManage() (e.g., GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup). That seems to broaden write access beyond manage scope and could allow unintended group modifications.

In hasPermission, when no group-specific resource exists you call getResourceTypeResource(...) and then immediately policyStore.findByResource(server, resource); if resource is null (schema not initialized / missing resource), this will NPE. Consider handling a missing resource-type resource by returning false.

golden: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
candidates: --flusher-processes accepts negative integers which can make SpanFlusher.num_processes invalid and crash shard-to-process mapping/modulo at startup - should enforce minimum of 1
Inconsistent metric tag key naming: timer uses 'shards' but produce timer/segment-size metric uses 'shard', which will split metric series and complicate dashboards

isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard may not match processes created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, causing hung children to not be killed before replacement and leaking flusher workers
When timeout elapses in join(), the break exits the loop without terminating remaining flusher processes, leaving background workers running during shutdown/rebalance
time.sleep(0.1) is patched to a no-op at the top of the test, so it doesn't actually wait for the flusher to observe the drift change, making the test timing-dependent/flaky on slower CI

golden: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

golden: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

golden: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
candidates: In website_name, the logic doesn't cover the case where the instance host is the apex domain (e.g. example.com) but the user website is a subdomain (e.g. www.example.com/user); in that case this branch returns only www.example.com without the path. Subdomains of the instance domain may need to include the path as well.

The conditional serializer helper is named include_website_name (missing ?) instead of include_website_name? like all other helpers, which means it won't gate serialization as expected and may cause website_name to be emitted unconditionally.

golden: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
candidates: The origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` can be bypassed by attacker-controlled origins that contain the Discourse URL as a substring (e.g., `https://discourse.example.com.evil.com`). Need stricter origin validation before trusting resize messages.

`postMessage`'s `targetOrigin` is set to `request.referer`, but browsers expect an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not a full URL with path/query. Passing the full referer can throw and break the iframe resize handshake.

Some feeds don't provide `content` for items; `i.content.scrub` will raise if `i.content` is `nil`, which would break polling. Need to guard/fallback to another field (e.g., description) before scrubbing/unescaping.

`url` is interpolated directly into an `<a href='...'>` inside a raw HTML string, so quotes or unexpected characters in the URL can break markup and potentially create an injection/XSS vector. Need to escape/sanitize the URL before embedding it into HTML.

When `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` and bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. If any imported content isn't strictly sanitized upstream (RSS or remote fetch), this can become an XSS vector on Discourse-rendered pages.

The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

The hardcoded 10MB limit for images likely shouldn't apply to attachment uploads
Using a fixed 10.megabytes download cap ignores SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and can cause instance configuration to be bypassed or prevent larger configured limits
The same 10MB constant is duplicated in multiple places, risking client/server limit drift

The downsize loop only shrinks to ~33% of the original after 5 iterations (0.8^5), so a 10MB image may still exceed max_image_size_kb and proceed to Upload.create_for despite the comment promising automatic reduction
If OptimizedImage.downsize fails and returns false, the loop keeps retrying and the oversized file continues

There are two self.downsize method definitions where the latter overrides the former and changes the signature, which will raise ArgumentError for callers still passing max_width, max_height (e.g. app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb)

golden: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
candidates: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys ([z.string().toString()]), which will literally create keys like "[object Object]" and won't validate arbitrary numeric expiry fields as intended; safeParse will likely fail for real token responses

parseRefreshTokenResponse switches to minimumTokenResponseSchema whenever credential sharing + sync endpoint are configured, even when the refresh call is still hitting the third-party provider (e.g., team credentials), so valid provider responses can be parsed against the wrong schema
Setting a missing refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" can overwrite a previously valid refresh token when callers merge/store .data, which would break subsequent refreshes

refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response when syncing is enabled but returns whatever refreshFunction() returns otherwise (axios/hubspot/google responses), so downstream code can break depending on env
res?.data assumes a Gaxios-style response, but when refreshOAuthTokens uses fetch it returns a Response without .data, so token.access_token/token.expiry_date will be undefined and refresh will fail
parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result object, so data: { key } would persist { success, data, ... } instead of the credential JSON payload
When syncing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a Response, but this code treats it as a HubspotToken and immediately reads expiresIn/accessToken, which will throw at runtime
refreshOAuthTokens's third argument is userId, but this call passes credentialId; if syncing is enabled it will POST the wrong calcomUserId and likely refresh the wrong account

appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse (and the subsequent JSON.parse) can throw and return a 500 for malformed requests; without a method guard this endpoint is also callable via non-POST methods
APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED resolves to a string/undefined (due to &&), not a boolean; any code that expects a strict boolean may behave unexpectedly
After refreshing and storing the new Salesforce access token, the jsforce.Connection is still initialized from the pre-refresh credentialKey values, so immediate API calls may use an expired token

golden: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.
candidates: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async but calls aren't awaited/collected, so reminder cancellations/DB updates can be lost if the handler returns before the promises settle

Because cancellations are processed after the earlier delete-by-date logic, if this cron runs late a cancelled reminder could be removed from DB without ever sending the corresponding SendGrid cancellation request

The SendGrid call assumes reminder.referenceId is always a valid batch id; if it's null/empty (or for non-email rows), this will throw and the reminder won't be deleted, causing repeated failures on subsequent runs

golden: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

golden: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
candidates: Component is exported as `function TwoFactor` even though it's a backup-code UI; the name mismatch can be confusing in stack traces/DevTools and when importing alongside the real `TwoFactor` component
`navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` isn't awaited/handled, so the success toast can show even if the clipboard write fails (e.g., permissions/unsupported environment)

Renders an `<a>` wrapping a `Button` that becomes a `<button>`, which creates nested interactive elements (`<a><button>…`). This can cause inconsistent click/keyboard behavior and is invalid HTML semantics

A new object URL is created for `backupCodesUrl`, but it's only revoked when generating a new one; if the modal is closed/reset without another setup run, the object URL can leak and keep the blob alive longer than intended

`JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` can throw (or return a non-array) if `backupCodes` is corrupted/unexpected, which would crash the authorize/disable flow with a 500. Consider guarding parse/decrypt errors and validating the decoded shape before using `indexOf`

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

golden: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
